projectDescription: An FPGA carrier board integrating a RISC-V FPGA with a 128-bit LPDDR4 memory bus. It includes USB-C for power input and an HDMI output for a GPU's display.

imagePromptSnapshot.description:
Project idea: Design a carrier board for a RISC-V FPGA (like an ECP5 or Artix-7) that includes a 128-bit wide memory bus to an LPDDR4 chip, a USB-C power input, and an HDMI output for the GPU's display.

Design notes: RISC-V FPGA, 128-bit memory bus, LPDDR4 memory, USB-C power, HDMI output

Electrical components (current): Main FPGA (mcu, 15x15x1mm); 10x module: LPDDR4 Memory Chip 0, LPDDR4 Memory Chip 1, LPDDR4 Memory Chip 2, LPDDR4 Memory Chip 3 +6 more; 6x power: FPGA Core Voltage Regulator, LPDDR4 VDD1/VDD2 Regulator, LPDDR4 VDDQ Regulator, LPDDR4 VPP Regulator +2 more

Mechanical/structural parts (current): 7x misc: PCB Standoff (Front-Left), PCB Standoff (Front-Right), PCB Standoff (Back-Left), PCB Standoff (Back-Right) +3 more; 12x 3d_printed: Bottom Enclosure Half, Top Enclosure Half, LPDDR4 Memory Chip 0 Mount, LPDDR4 Memory Chip 1 Mount +8 more

Assembly: PCB Standoff (Front-Left) → Bottom Enclosure Half (M3 screws); PCB Standoff (Front-Right) → Bottom Enclosure Half (M3 screws); PCB Standoff (Back-Left) → Bottom Enclosure Half (M3 screws); PCB Standoff (Back-Right) → Bottom Enclosure Half (M3 screws); Bottom Enclosure Half → Top Enclosure Half (enclosure_assembly_screws); LPDDR4 Memory Chip 0 Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws); LPDDR4 Memory Chip 1 Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws); LPDDR4 Memory Chip 2 Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws); LPDDR4 Memory Chip 3 Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws); HDMI Transmitter Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws); USB-C PD Controller Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws); USB-C Power Input Receptacle Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws); HDMI Type-A Output Receptacle Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws); JTAG Debug Header Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws); FPGA Configuration Flash Mount → Bottom Enclosure Half (M2 screws) (+11 more connections)

originalPrompt: Design a carrier board for a RISC-V FPGA (like an ECP5 or Artix-7) that includes a 128-bit wide memory bus to an LPDDR4 chip, a USB-C power input, and an HDMI output for the GPU's display.
plan:
- Core Electrical: RISC-V FPGA (Lattice ECP5 or Xilinx Artix-7), LPDDR4 memory ICs, HDMI transmitter IC, USB-C Power Delivery (PD) controller.
- Power Management: Multiple DC-DC converters for FPGA core/IO, LPDDR4, and peripheral voltages; power sequencing circuitry.
- Connectivity: USB-C receptacle for power input, HDMI Type-A receptacle for video output, JTAG/debug header, expansion headers (e.g., PMODs, GPIO).
- Board Design: Multi-layer PCB (8-12 layers) with impedance-controlled routing for LPDDR4 data/address bus and HDMI differential pairs.
- Mechanical: Custom PCB design, surface-mount and through-hole components, standoffs for mounting.

assumptions: Basic surface-mount soldering experience, including fine-pitch components
Familiarity with 3D printer operation and maintenance
Understanding of digital logic and embedded systems
Access to a host PC with FPGA development tools and drivers installed
USB-C Power Delivery (PD) compatible power supply for testing

subSteps.title: 3D print bottom and top enclosure halves
3D print all LPDDR4 memory chip mounts
3D print HDMI Transmitter and receptacle mounts
3D print USB-C PD Controller and receptacle mounts
3D print JTAG Header and SPI Flash mounts
Inspect and deburr all 3D printed parts for optimal fit and clear openings
Solder FPGA (ECP5) to the PCB
Solder all LPDDR4 Memory Chips to the PCB
Solder HDMI Transmitter and Configuration Flash to the PCB
Solder USB-C PD Controller and all voltage regulators to the PCB
Solder USB-C and HDMI Type-A receptacles, and JTAG header to the PCB
Visually inspect all solder joints for bridges, shorts, and cold joints
Perform continuity checks on all power and ground rails to ensure no shorts
Apply initial power via USB-C and verify all regulator output voltages
Connect JTAG programmer and verify FPGA recognition
Program FPGA configuration flash with initial bootloader/test bitstream
Develop and load a basic test bitstream for LPDDR4 memory interface to verify connectivity
Develop and load a basic test bitstream for HDMI output to verify display signal
Verify I2C communication with USB-C PD controller and HDMI transmitter
Mount the FPGA heat sink onto the FPGA with thermal paste/pad
Mount all electrical components into their respective 3D printed mounts
Secure the PCB into the bottom enclosure half using PCB standoffs and M3 screws
Fasten all component mounts to the bottom enclosure half using M2 screws
Attach the top enclosure half to the bottom enclosure half using assembly screws
Perform final system power-on and functional test to confirm stability and operation
